title: Mara and the Uniform
premise: During the closing winter of a forgotten continental war, battlefield nurse Cyrus Pemberton — born Mara, wearing a dead brother's uniform to serve — secretly records the names of soldiers the officers' official ledger omits. When a sealed letter implicates her adoptive regiment's command in a massacre being rewritten for the history books, Cyrus must choose between the anonymity that has kept her alive and the testimony that could condemn her. Racing the victors' historians to the armistice, she smuggles her ledger to a war correspondent, sacrificing her cover, her safety, and the quiet love of surgeon Elias Vane, who must decide whether duty or truth will claim her. The book ends with the truth published under the name Mara Pemberton — her own, at last — as she and Elias, both stripped of rank, walk away from the victory parades into an ordinary, hard-won life.
about_author: Dominic Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging soldiers' letters and unclaimed regimental ledgers. His fiction is known for excavating the quiet clerical heroism that grand military histories leave out.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus Pemberton. In a freezing field hospital, Cyrus tends the wounded by day and, by candlelight, records in her hidden ledger the names of the dead the officers' reports omit — including, carefully, the men who might notice her disguise. Her only confidant is surgeon Elias Vane, whose lingering glances unsettle the anonymity she depends on. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of routine and the ache of being unseen even by the man she's growing to love.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus, with a brief interlude from Elias. A dying courier presses a sealed letter into Cyrus's hands: evidence that Colonel Ashe ordered the burning of a village of surrendered civilians — a massacre already being erased from the official record. When the letter's existence becomes known, suspicion falls on the hospital staff, and Cyrus realizes the ledger in her trunk could hang her as a spy. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into resolve; invisibility is no longer protection.

chapters.title: What the Victors Burn
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus and Elias in alternating chapters. As Ashe's men ransack the hospital and armistice negotiations signal the war's end, Cyrus and Elias race to copy and authenticate the ledger before it can be seized. Elias is offered a promotion — and his career — in exchange for handing her over; duty and love collide in a lantern-lit surgery where he chooses to forge her travel papers instead. Emotional beat: the climax of sacrifice, as both abandon the identities the war built for them.

chapters.title: Mara Pemberton, Attested
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Disguised as a war correspondent's widow, Mara delivers the ledger and the letter to a neutral-city press office hours before the victors' historians publish their sanitized account. The massacre makes the record; Ashe faces inquiry; Cyrus Pemberton vanishes into the archives of the war. Signing her own name for the first time in years, Mara reunites with Elias outside the city gates. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — truth survives, but only at the cost of everything they were.
